eli: Quick heads-up — perfetto trace (link below) shows a repeating HBM bandwidth waveform that lines up with KV prefetch bursts when seq_len > 4096. Looks like periodic oversubscription rather than steady-state saturation. https://perfetto.company/reports/abcd1234

marta: Saw that. Can you drop the nsys timeline? Curious whether kernels line up with the waves or if it's DMA/PCIe queuing.

eli: Pushed an nsys capture to GCS: gs://redwood-perf/nsys/2112345678.nsys. Quick grep shows spikes in HBM read BW ~ 180 GB/s for ~40ms windows, then a quiet 120 GB/s.

kevin: Replayed the trace locally — kernel dispatch timing shows synchronized prefetch + cross-block KV reads at the start of long sequences. Kernel heatmap: many small memcpy-ish kernels firing in a tight loop.

aj: Hypothesis: batching heuristics create microbatch groups that trigger prefetcher across many streams simultaneously. Two levers: stagger prefetch start time per microbatch OR cap total outstanding prefetch bytes.

eli: Agreed. I instrumented the batcher to introduce a jittered delay (rand(0..2ms)) before issuing prefetch. Re-ran nsys. Wave amplitude reduced ~35% and tail latency improved for heavy seqs.

kevin: Paste from the nsys summary I grabbed (trimmed):
```
CPU total time: 12.3s
HBM read peak: 182.4 GB/s (40ms window)
HBM read baseline: 118.9 GB/s
KV-prefetch kernels: 342 calls @ avg 120us
Small memcpy kernels: 4.8k calls
```

marta: Nice. Did the jitter patch affect throughput? We need to keep tokens/sec for hosted SLA.

eli: Throughput dip was ~2.7% in synthetic long-seq test, but p50 reduced by ~18ms for loaded p99. Trade-off looks good for customer-visible latency.

aj: Alternative less-invasive change: add a global prefetch_budget_bytes that enforces a simple accounting check before launching a prefetch. If outstanding_prefetch + request_size > budget -> queue. Budget default 64MB.

kevin: I tried budget=64MB locally; HBM waveform became flatter but microbursts still present on tail. Combined budget + jitter flattened it best.

eli: Patch candidate: default prefetch_budget_bytes=64MB, jitter_ms=1, and an opt-in env var REDWOOD_PREFETCH_THROTTLE=1. Putting PR up with benchmarks.

marta: Please include nsys/perfetto links and a short reproduction script in the PR. Also add a small e2e that asserts no sustained HBM >160GB/s for >100ms in our long-seq sim.

eli: Will do. PR in ~2h. Repro steps I'm adding to the PR: `scripts/trace_long_seq.sh --model gptx-large --seq 8192 --concurrency 8 --capture nsys`

perf-bot: nsys job finished: job_id=jk-9001, artifact=gs://redwood-perf/nsys/2112345689.nsys :white_check_mark:

kevin: One more note — kernel selection logic still picks a memcpy-optimized path for the KV page folds. If we can fuse a couple of small copies into a single kernel for large seqs, we might eliminate thousands of tiny dispatches and reduce driver overhead. Something for follow-up RFC.

aj: Agreed — I'll prototype a fused-prefetch kernel next week. For now merge the throttle+jitter and let's monitor host metrics for a week. :thumbsup:

eli: Thanks team, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/pull/4832 (benchmarks + traces attached)

marta: Looks great. After merge, schedule a canary on dedicated pools with long-seq traffic and watch HBM and latency.

kevin: Added a Perfetto marker in the runtime logs at prefetch start/end to help correlate next traces.

eli: Closing thread once PR merges. Thanks all. :rocket:
